note: Checked 24 September 2026. Re-check terms before each public release.

bluebook.label: Project Blue Book
bluebook.series: Sanitized Version of Project Blue Book Case Files on Sightings of Unidentified Flying Objects, 1947 to 1969 (NAID 597821)
bluebook.access: Download the JSON metadata only. It lists every digital object; fetch just the first page (the record card) of each case file. The full image zips run to hundreds of gigabytes, so avoid them.
bluebook.licence: US federal record, generally public domain. Attribute NARA.
bluebook.attribution: Project Blue Book case files, US National Archives (NAID 597821)
bluebook.scale: 12,618 sightings investigated 1947 to 1969, 701 concluded unidentified (the Project Blue Book programme total, per the US Air Force and National Archives Foundation); the sanitised series NAID 597821 itself holds 10,622 digitised file units (confirmed via the catalog's own fileUnitCount), since its own scope note says a case file can cover one sighting or a group of closely related sightings
bluebook.quirks: Scans are online out of chronological order. Witness names are already removed in the sanitised series.

geipan.label: GEIPAN
geipan.access: geipan.fr's own export endpoints, https://geipan.fr/fr/cnes/export/cas (cases) and https://geipan.fr/fr/cnes/export/temoignages (testimonies). Both endpoints serve XLSX despite their historical CSV naming, and both need a browser user agent: the default curl user agent gets a 429. Convert to CSV locally (cas_pub.csv and temoignages_pub.csv) into local_data/raw/geipan/ before the adapter reads them, and read the data dictionary before mapping columns.
geipan.licence: Published open data; confirm the reuse notice on geipan.fr before redistribution and attribute GEIPAN/CNES.
geipan.grades: A identified, B probably identified, C insufficient data, D unidentified after investigation

pursue.label: PURSUE (US Department of War)
pursue.access: Six releases so far (8 May, 22 May, 12 June, 10 July, 7 August, 18 September 2026), roughly 447 files. The site blocks automated clients, so download release bundles in a normal browser into local_data/raw/pursue/<release>/.
pursue.licence: US government work, generally public domain. Check each file for third-party material before republishing media.
pursue.attribution: PURSUE release files, US Department of War

ukmod.label: UK Ministry of Defence UFO files
ukmod.access: Files in the DEFE 24 and DEFE 31 series; about 209 files, 52,000 pages and 11,000 reports up to 2009. Download PDFs from TNA Discovery into local_data/raw/ukmod/.
ukmod.licence: Crown copyright; reuse under the Open Government Licence where TNA marks it so. Attribute The National Archives.
ukmod.attribution: Ministry of Defence UFO files, The National Archives (UK)

nuforc.label: NUFORC
nuforc.access: Only with written permission from NUFORC (support@nuforc.org). Their terms, updated 19 August 2026, forbid redistribution in any format and forbid downloading third-party copies, which covers the Kaggle, Maven Analytics and CORGIS sets (all derived from the same 2014 scrape).
nuforc.licence: Proprietary. Use only under the licence NUFORC grants, and store that licence alongside the data.
